title: The Golden Circle Comes to Tea

pages.text:
*From the Dropout Club Handbook, Rule 8: Never invite a Golden Circle student to anything with a floor that can open.*

The wind picked up, rattling the flowerpots on the shelf. It was a stiff, chilly breeze that made the dust dance in the air, but when the Potting Shed door creaked open, it did not touch the hair of the boy standing on the threshold.

Cassius Pomeroy stood there, his golden hair slicked back so smoothly it looked like it had been poured from a mold. Behind him stood Dahlia, with her long braids of gold beads, and Rex, whose round glasses reflected the muddy yard. Their cloaks were trimmed in gold, not a single wrinkle visible, and their shoes were so shiny they could have been used to check for a spot on a face.

Cassius looked around the shed. He sniffed, a tiny, precise motion that suggested the smell of wet earth and old manure was personally offending him.

"How cozy," he said, his voice smooth as polished stone. "Like a hamster cage."

He reached into his blazer pocket and pulled out a card. It was gold-edged and thick, heavier than a book. He held it out to Marnie with two fingers, as if it might be contagious.

"You are invited," he said, "to watch the Founders' Day ceremony from the very back. Please do not bring anything that squeaks."
pages.image: Cassius Pomeroy, a boy with perfect slicked golden hair and a royal-blue blazer, stands in a muddy shed doorway holding a gold card, while Dahlia and Rex stand behind him in pristine gold-trimmed cloaks, looking down at Marnie, an eleven-year-old girl with copper-red buns and a green cloak, who stares at the card in shock.

pages.text:
Marnie did not take the card. She kept her wand at her side, feeling the wood warm and solid against her palm while the wind rattled the broken pots behind her.

Cassius’s gaze slid past her to Toby, who was attempting to look casual by leaning against a shelf of chipped terracotta.

"I hear your magic is... unique," Cassius said, smiling with his mouth but not his eyes. "You say 'Light,' and it goes dark. How... irregular."

Toby adjusted his gold-rimmed glasses, a precise, deliberate motion. "It’s a matter of perspective."

Then the golden eyes landed on Lulu, who sat on a crate with her knees pulled tight to her chest. A heap of lavender-scented socks spilled from her lap, a tangled mess of stripes and polka dots.

"A laundry," Cassius observed, tilting his head. "How modern. Do they match?"

Lulu shrank into her orange hoodie. "I’m so sorry, I didn’t mean to..."

"Is he supposed to be indoors?" Cassius interrupted, nodding at Bunt, who had been carefully balancing a shortbread biscuit on his massive grey-green nose. The troll stopped chewing.

But it was when Cassius turned to Gerald that Marnie’s temper flared.

"And that," Cassius said, pointing a silver wand at the bird. "That unfortunate hat. I assume you are trying to straighten it?"

Gerald opened his orange beak. He did not honk. He hissed, a loud, sizzling sound that shook the air like a kettle boiling over. Rex dropped his glasses. They clattered onto the floorboards. Cassius blinked, his perfect smile faltering for just a second.
pages.image: Inside a cluttered shed, Cassius points a wand at Gerald with a purple starred ribbon, who is hissing aggressively; behind Cassius, Rex has dropped his round glasses on the wooden floor, and Lulu, in an orange hoodie, looks horrified, while Bunt holds a biscuit in his large hand.

pages.text:
Cassius straightened his blazer, refusing to acknowledge the fallen glasses or offer an apology. Instead, he reached into his other pocket and produced a notebook bound in gold leather, thick, heavy, and smelling faintly of cinnamon.

"Since you are invited to witness the Founders' Day," he said, snapping the cover open with a sharp crack, "I shall explain the showpiece. My invention. The Perfectly Perfect Spell."

He turned the page, revealing script that was tiny, elegant, and terrifyingly neat.

"It will make every last thing at Humbleton flawless," he explained, his voice rising with pride. "No wobbles. No mistakes. No... irregularities." He looked at Marnie. "It will last forever. The Principal has approved it as the centerpiece of the ceremony."

Marnie watched his hand. For half a second, just a flicker, his fingers trembled. He looked at the shaking hand, then back at the group, and smiled so hard his cheeks hurt.

"Steady as a rock," he said. "Precise as a clock."

Toby watched the trembling hand, watched it stop, and watched Cassius close the book with a force that cracked the gold clasp.

"It is not a clock," Toby said quietly. "It is a very large soap bubble."
pages.image: Cassius holds open a thick gold notebook, his hand visibly trembling slightly, while Marnie, Toby with gold glasses, and Lulu watch with worry; the shed is dim, with flowerpots in the background, and the light focuses on the golden book and Cassius's intense, proud face.

pages.text:
Bunt sniffed.

It was a small sound at first, a polite little noise that happens right before you scratch an itch, but Bunt’s nose was enormous, and the air in the shed was thick with the scent of wet soil, old manure, and Lulu’s lavender socks.

"Ah..." Bunt started.

Cassius frowned and turned around. "What is it, you large..."

"Ah... ah... AH-CHOO!"

The sneeze hit like a full-scale hurricane made of sneezes. It was a gale that swept across the shed, blowing dust into the corners and knocking over a stack of empty jars. It struck Cassius squarely in the chest.

The golden shimmer in the notebook died. The light reflecting off the pages vanished. And then, for the first time in recorded history, Cassius Pomeroy’s hair flopped. It fell forward, covering his eyes, his nose, and his mouth. He looked, for a brief and terrible moment, like a child who had just lost a very bad fight with a hairbrush.

Cassius shrieked. He grabbed Dahlia’s hand. Dahlia grabbed Rex’s sleeve.

"Out!" Cassius shouted. "Get out of this... this... shed!"

They bolted for the door. Rex, still blind without his glasses, stumbled into the doorframe. Cassius, in his shiny black shoes, lost his grip on the muddy ground.

*Whoosh.*

The entire Golden Circle slid down the muddy slope outside, a bright streak of gold and blue, until they hit the bottom with a thud and a shower of mud.
pages.image: Three students in gold-trimmed cloaks slide down a muddy hillside, their shiny shoes skidding; Cassius's golden hair is messy and flopped over his face; Bunt, a tall grey-green troll, stands in the doorway with a huge red-spotted handkerchief, looking surprised, while Gerald honks from the side.

pages.text:
When the dust settled, the shed was quiet, save for the ticking of the stove clock and the sound of Lulu picking up a lavender sock.

Toby walked to the spot where a page had fallen, his polished shoes careful on the mud, and picked up the single page that had torn loose and flapped against the floorboards. He smoothed it flat with the precision of a surgeon, though his hands were trembling slightly.

He read the last line, and his face went pale.

"It says..." he whispered, adjusting his round gold glasses. "It says it requires a balance."

He looked up at the others. "And then there is a word. It is scribbled out. He crossed it out."

"He crossed out the balance?" Marnie asked, leaning closer.

"He crossed out everything," Lulu said softly, holding her sock up like a trophy. "He made it perfect. But there is no perfect without... without the rest."

"We should tell the teachers," Toby said, his voice thin and reedy. "Now. Immediately."

"They won’t listen to dropouts," Marnie said, and her voice was flat as a pancake left out in the rain.

Toby looked at her. He looked at Lulu, who was still holding the sock. He looked at Bunt, who was still wiping his nose with a handkerchief the size of a beach towel.

"Then we’ll watch," Marnie said, crossing her arms. "If something goes wrong..."

Toby straightened his red bow tie, the fabric crisp against his navy vest.

"We’ll know exactly who to blame," he said. "And exactly what to do."

He should not have said it. But he did. And for a moment, none of them smiled.
pages.image: Marnie, Toby, Lulu, and Bunt stand in the muddy shed, looking down at a gold notebook on the floor; Toby holds a torn page, his expression serious; Marnie has her arms crossed, looking determined; the shed is dim, with rain starting to leak through the roof, creating a tense atmosphere.
